reviewers.recoveryContractMimeRestorationAndLogHan: e2e; independent file-only review reported with matching source hashes

scope: Independent source-only review of the CP2-10 runner and its isolated target/preservation guards. No module import, test, process probe, HTTP, Auth, SMTP, SQL, runtime mutation, password change, or credential generation was performed by this review.

originalCase.expected: Old password denied, new password accepted, valid recovery token consumed, and no secret in ordinary logs. Actual execution is required.

guardsReviewed: Explicit parent release and synthetic-only confirmation are required before network or SQL actions.
Private target/config/readiness/SMTP files must be regular, non-symlinked, mode 0600-equivalent, and remain under the resolved task runtime directory.

API 60321, separate GoTrue 60327, SMTP 60325, and PostgREST 60323 belong to the new UUID database on local PostgreSQL 55322; the original database is separately fixed to postgres. No request is directed to original Auth 55321.
Auth database DSN, external API/site URL, SMTP endpoint, binary/config/readiness/gateway hashes, exact listener PIDs, mapped executable, and SMTP identity are checked before and after the operation.
Every returned access token must belong to the selected existing synthetic owner, and its session_id must exist in auth.sessions in the isolated new database.

All public tables in both databases are compared by full-row count/digest, and original Auth users/sessions/refresh_tokens are additionally protected. All direct SQL in this runner uses BEGIN READ ONLY.
Only the two existing synthetic recipients are accepted; each recovery message must be a new private MIME receipt with exact recipient, sequence, bytes, SHA, and loopback-origin validation.

Temporary password and issued sessions remain in a private restoration checkpoint. The contract restores the original synthetic password in finally; fallback administrative repair is restricted to the selected owner in the isolated clone.

Ordinary Auth/SMTP log inspection compares secret values only in memory and publishes counts without raw messages, matching excerpts, or values. Intentional private MIME, checkpoint, and env files are outside that ordinary-log claim.
Final protected-row and source/config binding checks must succeed before the execution report can claim completeness.
limitations: This preparation review is not evidence that recovery succeeded, that the token was consumed, or that ordinary runtime logs contain no secrets; those require the owner execution report.
This review does not approve or infer hosted Supabase behavior, external email delivery, new credentials, access grants, or original-instance mutations.
A source/config change after these pins requires a new comparison; no blanket approval or raw diagnostic suppression is inferred.
